newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up despite fall in late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up despite fall in late Tokyo.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher despite weak consumer demand and a late fall in Tokyo futures, traders said.
"There was hardly anything to move the market today," said a dealer. "I think the higher price is just a technical adjustment."
Traders said the market acted like a typical Monday, with buyers content to just monitor prices.
"China and Europe are sidelined but may come in if prices soften," said a dealer, who added that October was usually a month of substantial activity before the run-up to Christmas.
Traders said fine weather in the last fortnight had led to ample supply of raw materials, which was also putting pressure on prices.
Dealers offered the SMR CV at 367 cents, SMR L at 348, SMR 5 at 317, SMR 10 at 307, SMR 20 at 306 and drum latex at 237.

At the close, October RSS 1 buyer rose 1.50 cents to 314 cents ($1.25) a kg. October SMR 20 buyer was also up 1.50 cents to 307.50. The INRO five-day average was down to 244.27 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 27 from 245.32 on Sept 26. The daily indicator was 242.11 against 242.74.
